sources.summary: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (last updated 12 Mar 2026): same-sex relations legal nationwide, no legal gender recognition, LGBTI organisations can register; the country ranks among the most 'accepting' in the region in perception indices and surveys show strong support for an anti-discrimination law, but a 2018 Social Weather Stations survey found only 22% of Filipinos supported same-sex civil unions and a majority opposed trans women's access to women's toilets; diversity-and-inclusion executive orders (2019, amended 2023) exist but were not implemented as of 2025; non-discrimination ordinances enacted at barangay, city, municipal and provincial levels, while national SOGIE legislation has been filed repeatedly since 1999 but never passed; Anti-Bullying Act 2013 and the Gender-Responsive Basic Education Policy (2017, reiterated 2022) cover SOGI in schools; Safe Spaces Act 2019 covers homophobic and transphobic slurs.

Bulatlat news (26 June 2025): an eighteen-year-old trans woman (Kierra Apostol, student of Cagayan State University, Peñablanca) was found dead in a Cagayan province river on 23 June 2025 with visible signs of physical assault; a person who admitted picking her up the previous night surrendered to police and denied killing her; the same piece records the killing of trans activist and former journalist Ali Macalintal by an unidentified gunman inside an acupuncture clinic in General Santos (23 June) and of Shalani Dolina in Caloocan earlier in 2025; a national LGBT alliance says the violence is 'proof that LGBT persons remain unsafe' and demands passage of the SOGIESC Equality Bill, stuck in Congress for 25 years (latest version filed 2022 as House Bill 5551 / Senate Bill 1600).
